newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toyota to build production line for 'hybrid' cars.
newsitem.headline: Toyota to build production line for 'hybrid' cars.

text.p: Toyota Motor Corp said on Monday it would build an assembly line for "hybrid" vehicles powered by gasoline and batteries at its plant in Aichi Prefecture, central Japan.
A company spokeswoman said it plans to introduce the vehicles before the end of this year.

She declined to give further details, but the Nihon Keizai Shimbun business daily reported at the weekend that Toyota plans to spend one billion to two billion yen on the new facilities and that they would have a production capacity of 1,000 vehicles per month.
The company will start building the production line in July, the paper said.
Hybrid cars will be equipped with 1500 cc engines, generators, nickel-metal hydride batteries and electric motors, it said.
The company earlier said it had developed a highly advanced hybrid power system for use in cars and would start selling cars using the system later this year.

Under the new system, called the Toyota Hybrid System, a gasoline engine, electric motor and electric generator are used to achieve nearly twice the fuel efficiency of conventional gasoline engine cars and drastically reduce exhaust emissions.
